column1: # Resource descriptions for the manual page and the web reference. One row per
# resource or numbered family. Names, classes, and literal defaults are checked
# against the widget's resource table; descriptions and types are by hand.

column7: description
Bitmap font for the Default entry of the VT Fonts menu, used when renderFont is false. Give an X logical font description or an alias known to xlsfonts(1).
Bitmap fonts for the Unreadable through Enormous entries of the VT Fonts menu, in that order. Shift+keypad plus and minus step through the configured slots by size.
Selects the Xft renderer (true) or the Xlib bitmap renderer (false). The value default behaves as true when faceName is set and false otherwise. The TrueType Fonts menu entry toggles it at run time.

Fontconfig pattern for the primary Xft face, for example "DejaVu Sans Mono" or "Hack:style=Regular". As in xterm the value may hold two comma-separated entries; the second is the first fallback. A size= field in the first entry overrides faceSize.
Point size of the Default entry when the Xft renderer is active. Sizes are resolved against the screen's Xft DPI so the physical size matches xterm.
Point sizes for the remaining VT Fonts menu entries. A zero value derives the size from the proportions of the corresponding bitmap font, as xterm does.
Xft face tried first for wide (double-width) text, and second for emoji when faceNameEmoji misses. The terminal engine decides cell width; this face only paints it.
Xft face tried first for clusters that resolve to emoji presentation.

Xft face tried for emoji characters that resolve to text presentation, such as a bare hammer and wrench, after the ordinary text faces and numbered fallbacks miss and before unnamed fontconfig candidates. The face is requested as monochrome, so a generic emoji rule cannot answer it with a color face. It never serves ordinary text, CJK or color emoji.
Xft face tried first for text-presentation characters whose base has the Unicode script property Han. Point it at the same face as faceNameDoublesize for a consistent CJK look.
Explicit bold face chain. With the Xft renderer an xft: entry names a fontconfig pattern for SGR bold; without it the bold style is derived from the primary face.
Explicit bold face chain for wide text, in the same form as boldFont.
Ordered user-supplied fallback faces consulted after the explicit role faces and before fontconfig's own candidates. Each holds one fontconfig pattern.
Permit unnamed fontconfig candidates after the named faces are exhausted. When false, a cluster no named face can draw is shown as a deterministic placeholder box.

Permit shrinking a monochrome face to fit a text-presentation emoji into the cells the terminal engine assigned it, instead of refusing the face because its glyphs are too wide. The scale is uniform and never enlarges, cursor movement is unchanged, and ink stays inside those cells. When false such a face is refused, as in earlier releases.
Budget of fallback faces that may be opened per font slot and style. Zero disables all fallback, including the second faceName entry and every fallbackFaceN.
Percentage tolerance applied when recognising a DEC double-height face. Accepted for xterm compatibility; double-height rendering is not implemented.
Percentage by which a fallback glyph's advance may exceed the cell before the face is rejected for that cluster.
Presentation for emoji without an explicit selector: unicode follows the Unicode default, text forces monochrome text presentation, emoji forces emoji presentation. VS15 and VS16 always win.
Permit colour glyph paint (CBDT, sbix, COLR, SVG). When false a face is used only if it has a genuine outline for the glyph.

Initial state of DEC private mode 2027. legacy keeps wcwidth-compatible cursor arithmetic; unicode enables grapheme-cluster width at startup and after reset. Applications may still set or reset the mode.
Collect bounded records of font routing decisions for the report-font-routing() action. Off by default because collection has a cost.
Default text colour.
Default background colour of the terminal widget, a core widget resource that also sets the scrollbar trough.
Text cursor colour. A focused block cursor is filled; an unfocused block is an outline.

The sixteen ANSI palette entries: color0 through color7 are the normal colours and color8 through color15 the bright ones. OSC 4 may change an entry at run time and OSC 104 restores the configured value.
Render bold text in palette colours 0 through 7 with the corresponding bright colour 8 through 15, as xterm does. When false, bold changes only the font weight.

Opacity of the default background from 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0. Takes effect only when a compositor owns the screen and an ARGB visual exists; otherwise the window starts opaque. Text, explicit cell backgrounds, the cursor, and menus stay opaque. The Opacity slider in the Main Options menu adjusts it at run time.
Swap the default foreground and background. Independent of the application-controlled DECSCNM mode and of SGR 7 inverse cells.
Lines of scrollback kept by the terminal engine. Zero disables history. The engine frees history in whole pages, so the limit is approximate within one page.
Show the Athena scrollbar. The scrollbar is an ordinary Xaw Scrollbar child named scrollbar, so its own resources such as width and thickness may be set through that path.
Place the scrollbar on the right instead of the left.
Border width of the scrollbar in pixels.
Jump to the live bottom when output arrives. When false the viewport keeps its distance from the bottom as new rows arrive.
Jump to the live bottom when a key is pressed.
Maximum interval in milliseconds between clicks of a double or triple click.

Character classes for double-click word selection, in xterm's low[-high]:class form separated by commas. Letters, digits, and underscore share class 48 by default; punctuation characters each form their own class.
Make the symbolic SELECT selection name mean CLIPBOARD instead of PRIMARY, for both copying and pasting.

The blanket permission for window operations that disallowedWindowOps would otherwise refuse, effective only while allowSendEvents is false. Revenant consults it for OSC 52 selection access (GetSelection, SetSelection), the XTWINOPS title reports and title stack (GetIconTitle, GetWinTitle, PushTitle, PopTitle) and the CSI 14/16/18 t size reports; other xterm window operations are not implemented. The Allow Window Ops menu entry changes it live, and is insensitive while allowSendEvents is true.

Comma-separated xterm window-operation names refused unless allowWindowOps is true and allowSendEvents is false; names are case-insensitive, accept shell-style * and ? wildcards, and a ~ prefix re-allows matches. Revenant consults GetSelection and SetSelection (OSC 52), GetIconTitle and GetWinTitle (XTWINOPS 20/21 reports), PushTitle and PopTitle (XTWINOPS 22/23), GetWinSizePixels and GetWinSizeChars (CSI 14/18 t), and GetScreenSizeChars, which gates CSI 16 t as in xterm; xterm's numeric codes 14, 18, 19 and 20-23 are also accepted, and 16 names nothing. The xterm default leaves OSC 52 and the title reports disabled while the title stack stays available.

Largest control string, in bytes, that the parser accepts. Revenant enforces it only for OSC 52 selection writes, measuring the base64 payload as xterm would; libghostty bounds every other control string itself.
Padding in pixels between the text and the window edge.
Initial number of columns when no geometry is given.
Initial number of rows when no geometry is given.

Initial size in characters and position in pixels, in the standard X form WIDTHxHEIGHT+X+Y, as in xterm. -geometry sets it. The size replaces columns and rows, and a zero size becomes one; negative offsets count from the right and bottom edges of the screen. When it is unset, the application geometry resource is read the same way, whereas xterm ignores the size given there.
Draw a filled block cursor even when the window does not have focus.

Configured cursor blink operand: false, true, always, or never. false and true combine with the application's DECSCUSR or mode 12 request under cursorBlinkXOR; always and never ignore the application. A reset restores this value.
Combine the configured and application blink states with exclusive or (true) or inclusive or (false), as in xterm.

Start with an underline cursor instead of a block; -uc and +uc set it. It takes precedence over cursorBar, and DECSCUSR 0, an omitted DECSCUSR parameter, or a full reset returns to it (xterm's CSI 7 SP q is not recognized). Blink is controlled separately by cursorBlink.

Draw supported procedural terminal glyphs from cell geometry instead of the font: box and block elements, Braille, DEC scan lines, terminal corner triangles, standardized legacy-computing symbols, and selected Powerline separators. +fbx sets it and -fbx clears it, as in xterm. When false the Xft path uses the primary face's own glyph and draws procedurally only when that face lacks the character; the bitmap path always draws supported ranges procedurally. The font menu's Procedural Glyphs entry and set-font-linedrawing() change it at runtime.
Start with a bar cursor instead of a block; -barc and +barc set it. cursorUnderLine wins when both are true, and DECSCUSR 0 or a full reset returns to the configured shape.
Text sent verbatim to the application when it writes ENQ (0x05). The default is empty, which sends nothing.
Milliseconds a blinking cursor remains visible.
Milliseconds a blinking cursor remains hidden.

Milliseconds that text just copied by a selection gesture flashes before returning to the ordinary selection highlight. 0 disables the flash. A new selection, losing or replacing the selection, and an application's OSC 52 write never start or extend it; the copied bytes are unchanged.
Background color of copied cells while copyFlashDuration runs. Empty by default, which shows the copied cells in their unselected colors for the flash instead.
Terminal name placed in the child's TERM and reported for an XTGETTCAP TN query, so both always agree; -tn sets it. Names over 128 bytes still set TERM but leave TN unanswered.

Skip a title or icon-name update that repeats the label last requested, so the window manager sees no redundant property change. The comparison is with the last request, not the live property, as in xterm, so a label another client changed is not rewritten by the same request. -samename and +samename set it.

Keep the window and its last output after the child exits, until the user closes it, as xterm -hold does. Input typed afterwards is discarded, and the terminal still exits with status 0. -hold and +hold set it.

Shell command started by pipe-command-output() (Ctrl+Shift+G by default) with the last completed command's output on its stdin, in the shell's last reported directory. Unset by default; the output is data and is never executed.
Locale under which the popup menus are created, so bitmap menu fonts work on UTF-8 desktops without charset warnings.
Minimum severity written to standard error: debug, info, warning, or error.
Compatibility alias: when logLevel is unset, true selects the debug level.
Print the resolved configuration report and exit instead of opening a window. Normally set with -report-config.
Window title. Applications may change it at run time with OSC 0 or OSC 2.
Icon name shown by the window manager.
Preferred position of the icon.
Start iconified.
Colour of the window border drawn by the shell.
Width of the window border drawn by the shell.

Allow application title changes and application of saved title/icon labels on pop. The Allow Title Ops menu and the allow-title-ops(on|off|toggle) action change this live. While allowSendEvents is true no label changes, whatever this value, and the menu entry is insensitive; the action still changes the configured value. Title reports and stack operations separately consult Window Ops. OSC 1 and the icon part of OSC 0 still lack libghostty callbacks.

The configured blanket permission for dynamic-color operations: OSC 10-19 sets and queries, OSC 110-119 resets, and OSC 4/5 palette queries. It permits every one of them only while allowSendEvents is false; when it is false, or while allowSendEvents is true, disallowedColorOps selects which operations are refused. The Allow Color Ops menu entry and the allow-color-ops(on|off|toggle) action change the configured value live.

As in xterm, true blocks Title Ops completely and blocks the blanket Color Ops permission. Only color operations not listed in disallowedColorOps stay permitted. allowTitleOps, allowColorOps and the allow-title-ops and allow-color-ops actions still change their configured values; the Allow Color Ops menu entry stays clickable, and the Allow Title Ops entry is insensitive. It also blocks the Window Ops blanket permission, so disallowedWindowOps alone decides, and the Allow Window Ops menu entry is insensitive. Unlike xterm, synthetic key and button events are accepted whatever the value, and the value is read only at startup.

Comma-separated xterm color-operation names refused unless allowColorOps is true and allowSendEvents is false: SetColor (OSC 10-19 sets and 110-119 resets), GetColor (OSC 10-19 queries), and GetAnsiColor (OSC 4/5 queries). Names are case-insensitive, accept * and ? wildcards, and a ~ prefix re-allows matches. Ordinary OSC 4 palette writes are never gated, as in xterm.

Permit application mouse and focus reports. The Allow Mouse Ops menu toggles this live; disabling restores local mouse selection without changing requested modes. Named disallowedMouseOps exceptions, locator and alternate-scroll policy are not yet implemented.

Permit terminal-capability operations regardless of disallowedTcapOps. The Allow Tcap Ops menu toggles this live; currently gates libghostty-generated XTGETTCAP replies, while XTSETTCAP is not implemented.
Case-insensitive operation names with wildcards and tilde negation, applied when allowTcapOps is false. GetTcap gates XTGETTCAP replies; SetTcap is reserved for future XTSETTCAP support.
Prepared permission for application OSC 50 font requests. No OSC 50 backend callback exists yet; the Allow Font Ops menu remains disabled and this resource has no font-changing effect.
Prepared font-operation restrictions for SetFont and GetFont, using case-insensitive names, wildcards and tilde negation. These restrictions have no operational effect until OSC 50 is connected.
